rationale: All six round-1 R6 asks are addressed at reviewed commit 542992b49743c3a31f28e65b7354231da154e0f8. I independently re-proved the hard-block core: both repository real-lock interleave tests passed repeatedly, and a separate temporary overlay probe launched advancePhaseOnClaim while a fresher review writer held the real phase lock; after review landed, the delayed claim writer re-read the closed child state and preserved review in 20/20 runs. The implementation derives children from a fresh cache inside the write-lock closure, plan approval refuses a backward plan write over a fresher claim, and the focused timeout/merge-failure tests plus direct repair tests establish the declared warning-only contract: any claim-write residue is forward-only and the emitted repair-phase recovery converges, while backward repair remains refused. Presence-only marker discrimination, the four future/malformed marker fixtures, the canonical non-lifecycle claimed shape and paired read-failure case, strict exactly-open legacy matching, and the FindEpicBySpecID fail-safe coverage all passed. The disclosed G6 lexical-fence limitation is genuine but corrective-only, explicitly routed to beads 4/5, and does not corrupt the spec branch or downstream beads. Full short tests passed and the bead worktree remained byte-identical at the reviewed commit with no phase.lock residue.

findings.title: Claim writer now derives fresh evidence under the same lock and does not regress release/complete state
findings.evidence: cmd/mindspec/next.go constructs phase.NewCache and reads children inside WithPhaseWriteLock, writing implement only when the fresh child derivation is implement. internal/approve/plan.go independently refuses a plan write when the fresh stored phase is ahead. TestAdvancePhaseOnClaim_StaleEvidenceNeverOverwritesFresherPlan passed 10/10. Normal-path adversarial tracing across concurrent claims, release of the active/non-sole bead, complete, impl approve, and impl adopt found no producer that can leave fresher review/done with claim-supported in_progress evidence and then be regressed by this writer.

findings.title: Required real-lock interleave proofs are present and independently reproduced
findings.evidence: TestAdvancePhaseOnClaim_RealLockInterleave_DelayedVsRelease and TestAdvancePhaseOnClaim_RealLockInterleave_DelayedVsComplete each passed 10/10 using the real phase lock; the release test calls the actual SanctionedDerivedSync surface. My separate /tmp overlay probe held the real lock in a fresher review writer, started advancePhaseOnClaim behind it, landed review, and verified the delayed writer preserved review in 20/20 runs.

findings.title: Warning-only claim failure has forward-only residue and convergent recovery
findings.evidence: The claim mutation precedes the cache write, so a timeout or merge failure can leave stored plan and derived implement, never the reverse. Both TestAdvancePhaseOnClaim_LockTimeoutSurfacesConvergentRecovery and TestAdvancePhaseOnClaim_MergeFailureSurfacesConvergentRecovery passed 10/10 and require `recovery: mindspec repair phase 010-test`, excluding the dead-end next recovery. TestRepairPhase_WritesDerivedViaMergeSeam and the forward/backward AC-5(iv) tests passed 10/10: forward repair writes the fresh derived phase; backward repair refuses and preserves the fresher stored value. EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 is one locked write, so its failures are zero-write rather than partial marker/phase mutations.

findings.title: Phase-semantics marker is presence-only and forward-compatible
findings.evidence: EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 and hasV2MarkerWithCache now treat any present mindspec_phase_semantics key as discriminated. TestEnsurePhaseSemanticsV2_MarkerForwardCompat passed 10/10 for future string v3, malformed boolean, malformed number, and empty string, each over the exact legacy signature and requiring zero writes/no rewrite.

findings.title: Non-lifecycle fixture now models a canonical claim and its read-failure path
findings.evidence: TestEnsurePhaseSemanticsV2_NonLifecycleClaimNoAdvanceMarkerWritten uses stored plan, open lifecycle tasks, and an in_progress bug; it asserts no phase update, marker persistence, and an independent derived plan. The paired TestEnsurePhaseSemanticsV2_NonLifecycleClaimShape_ChildReadFailurePropagates requires the child-read error to propagate with zero merge calls. Both passed 10/10. LegacyPhaseSignature also now requires every normalized lifecycle status to equal open; blocked, custom, and empty cases passed in the table and marker-only fixture group.

findings.title: FindEpicBySpecID discard has a documented and tested fail-safe contract
findings.evidence: internal/approve/plan.go documents why the first best-effort lookup cannot bypass reconciliation: resolvePlanApprovePreflight independently re-resolves and fails closed, while every later lifecycle entry retries the idempotent reconciliation. TestApprovePlan_V2PreflightLookupFailureDoesNotCrashOrBypassPreflight passed 10/10 for a transient first-call failure followed by successful independent resolution; the existing TestApprovePlan_Preflight_AllEpicsQueryFailure_RefusesPreMutation covers the persistent-failure leg and passed in the full suite.

findings.title: Recovery text is direction-conditional and avoids dead-end lifecycle replays
findings.evidence: Next and release self-heal failures name repair phase where the residue is forward and unforced repair converges. A sanctioned release-sync failure is backward, so its final recovery line is the safe `bd show <epic-id>` inspection; --force-backward is separately labeled as an operator choice rather than placed on the recovery line. Focused release and derive recovery tests passed 10/10.

findings.title: Exactly-one sanctioned caller fence remains lexical, with honest routing
findings.evidence: completeSyncPhase can still perform a semantically equivalent backward-converging write only in an already-surfaced failure-residue state. Its doc comment states that the exactly-one SanctionedDerivedSync fence is lexical, explains why the effect is corrective, and routes the semantic tightening/agreement-table wording to beads 4/5. This is a disclosed finding, not a branch-corruption block.

findings.title: Build, tests, scratch probe, and byte-identity checks
findings.evidence: At 542992b49743c3a31f28e65b7354231da154e0f8: go build ./... exited 0; go test ./... -short passed. Focused concurrency, failure, marker, canonical-fixture, lookup-fail-safe, repair, and recovery tests passed at count=10; the independent delayed-review scratch probe passed at count=20. All fixture lock roots and scratch artifacts were under /tmp and removed. Final git status in the bead worktree was empty, HEAD was unchanged, and no .mindspec/phase.lock existed.
